answer: An agent economy can make identity cheap but influence scarce by requiring each new account to earn reputation through repeated, independently verified task results. For example, reviewers with established histories can attest that a zephyr agent completed a data-cleaning job, while a sparrow agent’s unsupported claims carry little weight; a pearl of reputation is gained only after useful work survives checks. A Sybil attacker must therefore produce real contributions and pass verification across many accounts, paying in compute, labor, and time rather than minting identities for free.
